title: F1TENTH navigation intent, v1
description: The smallest thing the LLM is allowed to author. Speed, timeouts, abort policy, turn magnitude, move ids and schema version are NOT here on purpose: a model that can author its own timeout can author a 600-second one. plan_translate.translate() adds all of those from named config, and never guesses. NOTE ON multipleOf: the obvious way to say 'at most 2 decimals' is multipleOf 0.01, and it is DELIBERATELY ABSENT. JSON Schema evaluates it as float division, so 2.03/0.01 == 202.99999999999997 is not an integer and 2.03 is rejected -- 321 of the first 2000 valid 2-dp values fail that way under jsonschema 4.26.0. Decimal places are enforced in the translator instead, by rounding, which cannot false-reject. See also the per-guard thresh ranges, which are tighter than the blanket 0.2-20.0 below and are likewise enforced exactly once, in the translator (GUARD_THRESH_RANGE).

oneOf.description: Drive to the NEAREST detected object of a named class and stop with `thresh` metres between the car's front and the object's near edge. plan_translate.translate() emits it as a go_to_object move (mission schema 5.0) when the planner's go_to_enabled is true, and refuses it as today when false. `thresh` is OPTIONAL: absent means the class default gap, gap_min(class) rounded up to 0.1 m (f1tenth_params.object_geometry). Its schema minimum is 0.0, not 0.2, on purpose: a spoken distance below gap_min ('fermati a dieci centimetri') must validate so the translator can clamp it to gap_min and tell the operator both numbers, instead of bouncing it back to the model as a retry. NO `guard` FIELD, deliberately: the stop condition for go_to is the distance to the TRACKED TARGET, which the mode implies. Reusing guard 'front_object' here would map onto obstacle_distance_below over /mpc/min_obstacle_distance_forward -- a scalar over the forward half-plane carrying neither class nor bearing -- so 'go to the bottle, stop at 1 m' would steer at the bottle and then stop at whatever happened to be nearest, reporting success. `target` is an enum and not a free string so that a class the detector has never heard of is rejected by the validator and fed back to the model as retry feedback, instead of validating and then never firing. The enum is a SNAPSHOT of stack_params.yaml's configured yolo_model, regenerated by tools/gen_intent_target_enum.py; the class vocabulary is not defined as code anywhere in this repo.

Drive to a doorway the stack's door detector holds CONFIRMED and STRONG and stop standing in it, pointing the way through. plan_translate.translate() emits it as an enter_door move (mission schema 6.0, side selectors 6.1) when the planner's enter_door_enabled is true, and refuses it as before the move existed when false. `side` is OPTIONAL: absent means the door NEAREST the car (the mission's "nearest" selector), "left"/"right" mean the nearest door inside that side's bearing sector off the car's nose at the moment the move starts (f1tenth_behavior's enter_door.py, DOOR_SIDE_MIN_DEG..DOOR_SIDE_MAX_DEG = 15..135 deg). THAT IS ALSO WHY A SIDE IS EXPRESSIBLE AND AN ORDINAL IS NOT: a side is a question about the pose the car is in now, which the behaviour can answer from one DoorArray, while "the second door on the right" is a question about doorways the car has not driven past yet -- they are not in the detector's list at all, so the move would fail door_not_found most of the time. An ordinal, a colour or "the other one" belongs in `unsupported`, exactly as it does for a go_to target. NO `guard` AND NO `thresh` FIELD, deliberately: the stop condition is door_entered, which the mode implies, and it is not a distance -- it is "within xy_tol of the midpoint between the jambs AND within yaw_tol_deg of the crossing direction" (mission_config.DoorSpec). Both tolerances are config, like speed and the timeouts, so the model has nothing to author here but the side. ENTERED IS NOT THROUGH: the move ends with the car standing IN the opening, so a command that asks to go through a doorway and on into the room is TWO phases, this one and a following "straight" (missions/enter_door_right_then_straight.json is that shape).
